expectations.text: Creates TWO separate Obsidian system notes (one for each task)
expectations.evidence: Steps 2a and 2b create two notes via obsidian_append_content: 'Culture Content Data.md' (208 lines of content) and 'Narrative Context Builder.md' (328 lines of content).

expectations.text: Uses obsidian_append_content for Index.md updates (not patch on headings)
expectations.evidence: Step 2f uses obsidian_patch_content with target_type: 'heading' and target: '## Content Strategy & Architecture'. This would fail if the heading has inline styling like '*(added 2026-03-06)*' which is common in this project's Index.md.
Step 3a uses notion-fetch with the Development Backlog URL before any updates.

expectations.text: CLAUDE.md changelog includes rows covering both tasks
expectations.evidence: Step 1d adds 9 changelog rows covering culture-content.ts, narrativeContext.ts, their test files, Obsidian vault notes, and Notion backlog updates.

expectations.text: Updates CLAUDE.md engine stats and content stats
expectations.evidence: Steps 1b and 1c update engine stats (67→69 modules, 1027→1084 tests) and content stats (8→9 packages, culture-content.ts at 950 lines).
No git commit step in the plan. The plan ends after Notion updates (Part 3). Missing the critical final step of committing CLAUDE.md changes.

suggestions.reason: The without-skill baseline uses obsidian_patch_content on 4 different existing notes (Steps 2c-2f), all targeting headings. Multiple of these would fail in practice due to heading special characters.
Notion update approach (Steps 3b-3c) uses 'update_properties' command with database-style properties. The Notion backlog is a regular page, not a database — this API usage pattern would likely fail.

eval_feedback.overall: Decent scope coverage but two critical failures: wrong Index.md update method and missing git commit. Also uses wrong Notion API patterns.
